links.outcome: Self-perceived AI evaluation competence and reported verification practices
links.effect: Self-perceived Evaluation scores increased from 3.45 (0.82) to 4.23 (0.61); d =0.93, 95% CI 0.73‐1.13, P <.001. Participants described cross-checking outputs; verification performance was not objectively assessed.
links.quote: In this study, improvements in the Evaluation and Ethics domains were mirrored by qualitative descriptions of deliberate verification, with students cross-checking AI outputs against trusted sources and supervisory judgment.

links.outcome: Self-perceived generative AI literacy following structured training
links.effect: Total self-perceived AI literacy increased from 3.57 (SD 0.64) to 4.23 (SD 0.54); Cohen d =0.98, 95% CI 0.77‐1.19, P <.001. Findings reflect immediate self-reported changes without a comparator.
links.quote: The mean total score increased from 3.57 (SD 0.64) preintervention to 4.23 (SD 0.54) postintervention ( t 138 =11.55, P <.001), corresponding to a large effect size (Cohen d =0.98, 95% CI 0.77‐1.19).

links.effect: Qualitative themes indicated a shift toward verification-oriented generative AI use, including calibrated trust through verification.
links.quote: Reflexive thematic analysis (interviews: n=6; reflections: n=17) identified five themes and one emergent theme describing a shift toward verification-oriented GenAI use: (1) understanding GenAI capabilities and limitations, (2) prompt-engineering skill development, (3) calibrated trust through verification, (4) GenAI-supported communication and collaboration, and (5) ethical considerations, with emerging reconceptualization of professional identity.
